title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement:
You are given the price of a stock on each of `n` consecutive days, where `prices[i]` is the price on day `i`.

You may complete **at most one transaction**: choose one day to buy one share and a **strictly later** day to sell it. You cannot sell before you buy, and you cannot hold more than one share.

Print the maximum profit you can make. If no transaction can make a profit, print `0` (that is, you may choose not to trade at all).
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers, the daily prices.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum profit, or `0` if no profit is possible.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 3 at price 2 and sell on day 4 at price 8 for a profit of 6. Buying at 4 on day 1 would only reach 8 - 4 = 4.
The price falls every day, so any trade loses money. The best choice is not to trade.
The lowest price is 1 on day 1, and the highest price after it is 9 on day 2, so the profit is 8. Later prices never beat that.

hints: Trying every buy day and every later sell day works but takes O(n^2) time.
If you fix the sell day, the best buy day is the cheapest price seen before it.
Scan once, keeping the minimum price so far and the best difference between the current price and that minimum.
